# Data Model: Normative/Advisory Detection (WI-33)

**Generated by**: `/speckit.plan` | **Date**: 2026-02-17

---

## Entity Overview

WI-33 introduces one new enum type (`Modality`), one new struct (`ModalityResult`), and extends one existing struct (`PolicyRequirement`). No new tables, files, or storage is added — this is a pure in-memory enrichment pass.

---

## New Types

### `Modality` Enum

**Location**: `src/model/mod.rs` (alongside `PolicyRequirement`)
**Exported from**: `src/lib.rs`

```rust
/// Classification of a policy requirement's obligation strength.
///
/// Derived from heuristic verb matching against RFC 2119 keywords.
/// Applied by WI-33 modality detection enrichment pass.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Modality {
    /// Mandatory obligation. Triggered by: "must", "shall", "will", "required".
    /// Also the default when no modality verb is detected.
    Normative,
    /// Recommendation or option. Triggered by: "should", "may", "recommended", "optional".
    Advisory,
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `Normative` | variant | Mandatory obligation language |
| `Advisory` | variant | Recommendation or optional language |

**Serialization**: `"normative"` or `"advisory"` (lowercase via `serde(rename_all = "lowercase")`)

**Validation rules**:
- Binary classification — no partial states
- Default when no modality verb detected: `Normative`
- When both normative and advisory verbs detected: `Normative` (strongest wins)

---

### `ModalityResult` Struct

**Location**: `src/parse/modality.rs` (internal to modality module)

```rust
/// Result of modality detection for a single policy requirement.
///
/// Provides the detected classification plus diagnostic metadata for
/// warning generation and audit logging.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ModalityResult {
    /// The detected modality classification.
    pub modality: Modality,
    /// All verbs matched in the requirement text (both normative and advisory).
    /// Empty only when `is_default` is true.
    pub matched_verbs: Vec<String>,
    /// True when no modality verb was found; default classification applied.
    /// Triggers a `tracing::warn!` when true.
    pub is_default: bool,
    /// True when both normative and advisory verbs were found.
    /// Normative classification applied (strongest wins).
    /// Triggers a `tracing::warn!` when true.
    pub has_conflict: bool,
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `modality` | `Modality` | Final classification |
| `matched_verbs` | `Vec<String>` | Verbs matched (for diagnostics) |
| `is_default` | `bool` | No verb found; default applied |
| `has_conflict` | `bool` | Both normative and advisory found |

## Extended Types

### `PolicyRequirement` (Extended)

**Location**: `src/model/mod.rs`
**Change**: Add `modality: Option<Modality>` field

```rust
/// An individual policy requirement extracted from a list item or clause pattern.
///
/// Requirements represent the atomic units of policy that will map to OSCAL controls.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]
pub struct PolicyRequirement {
    // ... existing fields unchanged ...
    pub stable_id: Option<String>,
    pub text: String,
    pub source_line: usize,
    pub nesting_depth: u8,
    pub atom_index: usize,
    pub parent_text: Option<String>,
    pub citations: Vec<Citation>,

    // NEW in WI-33:
    /// Modality classification: normative (mandatory) or advisory (recommended).
    /// - `None` until populated by WI-33 modality detection pass
    /// - `Some(Modality::Normative)` or `Some(Modality::Advisory)` after annotate_modalities runs
    /// - Defaults to `Some(Modality::Normative)` when no modality verb detected
    pub modality: Option<Modality>,
}
```

**Default value**: `None` (consistent with `stable_id: None` pre-WI-7 pattern)

**Impact on existing code**:
- Struct initialization in tests: all `PolicyRequirement { ... }` literals must add `modality: None`
- Snapshot tests: OSCAL JSON output will include modality props — snapshots require update
- `PartialEq` derive: unchanged (field included in equality)
- `Serialize` derive: `Option<Modality>` will serialize as `null` or `"normative"`/`"advisory"` if included in domain model output. The OSCAL output is controlled separately via the prop emitter.

## OSCAL Output Model

The `modality` field produces an OSCAL `prop` element in the output JSON. This is NOT a new Rust struct — it reuses the existing `OscalProp` defined in `src/oscal/parts.rs`.

### Prop Format

```json
{
  "name": "modality",
  "value": "normative"
}
```

or

```json
{
  "name": "modality",
  "value": "advisory"
}
```

**No `ns` field**: Modality is a semantic annotation, not a FORGE trace property. It does not use the FORGE trace namespace.

### Catalog Output Location

```json
{
  "catalog": {
    "groups": [{
      "controls": [{
        "id": "POL-AC-001",
        "props": [
          { "name": "modality", "value": "normative" }
        ]
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

### Component Definition Output Location

```json
{
  "component-definition": {
    "components": [{
      "control-implementations": [{
        "implemented-requirements": [{
          "props": [
            { "name": "modality", "value": "advisory" }
          ]
        }]
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

## State Transitions

```
PolicyRequirement.modality
    None                        (initial — before WI-33 runs)
       │
       ▼  annotate_modalities()
    Some(Modality::Normative)   (normative verb found, OR no verb found / default)
    Some(Modality::Advisory)    (advisory verb found only)
```

Once `annotate_modalities` runs, all requirements have `Some(modality)`. The pipeline guarantees this by running the enrichment pass before OSCAL generation.

---

## Classification Logic

```
Input: requirement.text
     │
     ├─ NORMATIVE_PATTERN matches?  → normative_hits: Vec<String>
     ├─ ADVISORY_PATTERN matches?   → advisory_hits: Vec<String>
     │
     ├─ normative_hits.not_empty AND advisory_hits.empty
     │     → Modality::Normative, matched_verbs = normative_hits
     │
     ├─ normative_hits.empty AND advisory_hits.not_empty
     │     → Modality::Advisory, matched_verbs = advisory_hits
     │
     ├─ normative_hits.not_empty AND advisory_hits.not_empty  [CONFLICT]
     │     → Modality::Normative, matched_verbs = normative_hits + advisory_hits
     │       has_conflict = true → tracing::warn!
     │
     └─ normative_hits.empty AND advisory_hits.empty          [DEFAULT]
           → Modality::Normative, matched_verbs = []
             is_default = true → tracing::warn!
```

---

## Verb Inventory

| Verb | Category | Pattern |
|------|----------|---------|
| must | Normative | `(?i)\b(must)\b` |
| shall | Normative | `(?i)\b(shall)\b` |
| will | Normative | `(?i)\b(will)\b` |
| required | Normative | `(?i)\b(required)\b` |
| should | Advisory | `(?i)\b(should)\b` |
| may | Advisory | `(?i)\b(may)\b` |
| recommended | Advisory | `(?i)\b(recommended)\b` |
| optional | Advisory | `(?i)\b(optional)\b` |

Combined into two patterns:
```
NORMATIVE: (?i)\b(must|shall|will|required)\b
ADVISORY:  (?i)\b(should|may|recommended|optional)\b
```
